correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts \(p^2\) and \(pq\). Prime squares fail by coprimality and size. For odd \(p<q\), \((q+1)/2\mid p(p-1)\) has only the two divisor placements used in the proof. The non-\(p\) placement is impossible modulo \(p+1\); the \(p\)-multiple placement reduces exactly to \(ab+2\mid b-4a-6\), whose sign and quotient cases \(t=1,2,\ge3\) are exhaustive. Only \(t=2\) survives and gives \(q=p^2-p-1\); the converse is verified by the exact quotient \(q(p-2)\).
